title: Investigate + patch: intermittent GPU OOMs and key-value cache index atomicity corruption during cross-tier traffic storms
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Customer-reported incidents across Hosted, Dedicated and Private stacks where high-throughput bursts from a mix of short-lived chat sessions and long-context embeddings triggered a cascade: GPU OOMs were observed concurrently with KV cache index corruption and worsening memory fragmentation. Symptoms varied by environment but shared a timeline: a sudden spike -> eviction thrash -> index write partials -> slab fragmentation -> OOMs on GPUs servicing large batches.

Why this ticket exists:
- Multiple customers escalated P0s over the last 48 hours (hosted latency spikes, 2 dedicated pools OOM, one private on-prem deployment saw degraded availability).
- Initial hotfixes (evictor tuning) reduced immediate OOMs but did not address intermittent KV index inconsistency that later caused request retries and customer-visible errors.
- We need a coordinated runtime patch that fixes atomicity in the KV compactor/journal write path, improves allocator behavior during mixed CPU/GPU allocation, and ships a staged rollout plus rollback plan.

Technical hypothesis / root cause (current):
1) Under mixed workload bursts the KV compaction step can interleave with async eviction: a race in the index metadata update commits a partial write (missing tombstone markers) which leaves a dangling slot referenced by sessions.
2) The allocator prefers large contiguous arenas for GPU-backed tensors; repeated partial frees cause slab fragmentation and an increase in small free fragments which prevents large contiguous allocations leading to GPU OOMs even when aggregate free memory is sufficient.
3) The runtime's background coalescer executes under the same priority as request handling which amplifies tail-latency; during spikes compaction runs at inopportune times causing CPU/GPU contention.

Immediate triage actions taken so far (short-term mitigations):
- Applied emergency throttle on hosted burst ingress and temporarily disabled background compaction on one affected dedicated pool (reduced new index partials).
- Backported a conservative allocator change to prioritize coalescing of small fragments when contiguous pages requested for GPU tensors are blocked (rolled to two dedicated nodes as a canary).
- Deployed request-level hedging for customers with high retry budgets to avoid live OOMs.
- Opened a retention-preserving trace capture for subsequent repros (trace IDs linked below).

Planned patch and rollout plan (this ticket's work):
- Code changes: 1) Make the KV index metadata update atomic by introducing a two-phase commit around tombstone updates and journal sync; 2) Adjust allocator to insert an opportunistic compaction hint when a large contiguous GPU allocation fails; 3) Lower background coalescer priority and add adaptive backoff based on allocation pressure signals.
- Tests: unit tests for index atomicity, heavy integration test that simulates mixed chat+embedding traffic, long-running chaos test for fragmentation under burst patterns.
- Canary rollout: runtime-1.24.3-hotfix -> 5% hosted canary + 2 dedicated pools (staggered) -> private customer opt-in -> full rollout. Monitor for OOM rate, KV index repair counts, compaction latency, and customer error rates.
- Rollback plan: revert runtime-1.24.3-hotfix and enable emergency allocator fallback (already built into runtime) to restore previous allocator behavior.

Observability / signals to monitor during rollout:
- KPI: GPU OOMs per shard, per-customer error rate, request P95/P99 latency, KV index repair/repair-failure counters, allocator fragmentation ratio (largest_free_contiguous / total_free).
- Dashboards: internal/runtime/gpu-ooms, internal/runtime/kvcache-integrity, internal/runtime/allocator-fragmentation (links below).

Customer comms and affected customers:
- Tier-1 customers A and B (hosted) reported increased timeout and error chatter; dedicated customer C had two OOM incidents; private on-prem customer D reported degraded throughput during a nightly job. Engineering lead has briefed support and solutions engineering to prepare mitigations.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Zero regressions in baseline perf (P95 latency within 5% of baseline) and at least 90% reduction in GPU OOMs on canary nodes under a replayed traffic spike.
- KV index atomicity test passes in CI and no index-repair events observed for 72 hours on canary.
- Post-rollout monitoring shows stable fragmentation metrics and no customer-facing errors.

Additional notes:
- This ticket coordinates work across runtime, allocator, and observability owners. We'll schedule a short runbook update and a postmortem within 72 hours of the full rollout.
